# Prismal Planning

> Prismal Planning (https://prismalplanning.org), formerly Prismal Budget, is a web budgeting app built around a calendar that shows five weeks at a time and looks years ahead. Each day lists its entries (costs and gains), and the budget projects "In Bank", the money in your budget's bank account at the end of every day, so negative days show up before they happen, and the lowest it gets as far past the calendar as you pick (2 months to start, up to a year). Home's calendar shows five weeks and moves to any five weeks from a year before the budget began to five years from today (past weeks show History's days), or lists them in List Mode, and it holds a calendar of your own too: Calendar Fractals (your calendars, each with its own name and color) whose entries can have times or be all day, with locations, travel time, repeats, alerts (push notifications before or after they start, any of them an alarm), notes, and other accounts they're shared with; each fractal is either the budget's (Per Budget, so everyone the budget is shared with sees it, and can change it with Can Edit on) or your own (in every budget, only yours unless you share it whole, each person with or without Can Edit), and an entry with a time keeps its time zone, so it shows at the right time when you travel, plus linked fractals that show another calendar's entries (read-only) and a Holidays fractal with the United States' holidays and other days widely kept; private links show them in Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, or Outlook, and a Quick Calendar home screen icon shows them (with the budget's linked calendars and Holidays) and adds entries with no login (each home screen icon, Quick Budget, Quick Calendar, or Snapshot, has its own picture and colors, picked with Customize). A Recipes tab keeps a budget's Pantry (each food's amount, unit, and expiration, with a shopping list everyone in the budget sees), its recipes, and the foods it uses, and its meals go on the calendar in a Meals fractal (filled in from a recipe, which a meal follows until it's changed); days whose meals the Pantry doesn't have enough for can glow orange, recipes it can't make can glow, and each meal's foods can come out of the Pantry on its day. Recurring entries fill themselves in, and so do entries from spreadsheets you connect (Google Sheets, Excel, and more, with a verified email) and paychecks worked out from a calendar of your work shifts, added under Automated Calendars & Paychecks (Apple, Google, Outlook, a work scheduling app, or another account's Calendar Fractal link, as paychecks, on your calendar, or both; or as costs, for someone you pay by their shifts: paydays, overtime, night pay, pay by event title, pay by time or day (weekend and night differentials), breaks, bonuses, deductions, and taxes from a percentage, a W-4, or any state's 2026 rates, with pay that changes over time); placeholders stand in for entries you expect (like an estimate) and are deleted once their day passes (or a day picked for them); any entry can have a note, as long as it needs to be, and one after today a reminder a number of days before it (a push notification or calendar event), and so can a recurring entry, before each day it lands on; an entry for an Equity account can be a percent of that account's balance; Bob, the budget's helper, has a page of cards you switch on as you like, each opening from a list (every account's balance on any day ahead, goals and what reaching them takes (how often and how much, with Add Recurring), Wavelength Planning, a spectrum of where your money goes across up to 10 wavelengths you name yourself, with Needs, Wants, and Future to start, plus Undefined, each entry on its own or its title's (Per Title), with goals per days, weeks, or months that Bob warns about at 85%, and a max for each wavelength shown as $250.00/$300.00 and 45%/50%, orange near it and red past it, and tips), whose warnings can show on Home, over the calendar, and whose Equity window says when each loan or card is paid off; a tracker (in Bob's figures) adds up spending by category between any two days, with a line graph of each category and its titles; a Spectrum Graph compares any accounts, categories, and other figures on one graph, where lines can be added together as one red or blue line; a Snapshot page shows the numbers and graphs you pick from anywhere on the site (In Bank, the lowest it gets, goals, accounts, gems, crystals, calendar entries, and every graph) as cards you add, drag into order, and can put on a phone's home screen (with your login, or as a no-login icon, after a warning, that only shows them and that Settings can turn off); Equity (in sections with their own totals, if you like; every budget has Savings and Cash; others, like a credit card, can have interest, with its rate, how it compounds, and the day it's added, kept in the balance or apart from it like a mortgage's, an escrow a mortgage's payment pays after its interest, and a Max) track money outside the budget's account, each listing every entry made on it, and transfers can move money between two of them; the Paycheck Calculator (with saved crystals) works out take-home pay, and the Accrual Calculator (with saved gems that goals can follow) shows when a loan or card is paid off, or when savings reach a goal, and what paying extra does; every change in the Change Logs has its own Undo, and opens what it changed, with changes from other devices highlighted; In Bank can show an Equity account (like another debit card), with its days below $0 red and its own lowest; Business Mode, on any one budget, adds a Business page (revenue, expenses, profit, asset purchases, assets, and owners, year by year), a Business choice in entry forms, and a Business card on Bob's page; budget and calendar entries can be copied to another day (holding one down, or right-clicking it, opens a quick menu: Edit, Move, Copy, Delete), a recurring payment into an Equity account can end Until $0, landing it on $0.00 exactly, and a budget can be given to someone it's shared with; an account can keep more than one budget, and share any budget it owns with other accounts, who join it and can then look at it, or with Can Edit on, change it too (Settings' Shared Users lists everyone; only its owner can share it on); devices with the same budget open, one person's or several people's, see each other's changes within seconds; Download My Data saves a copy of everything, and Upload A Backup brings a budget back from one, part by part; and as anything comes close to its limit (a part of the budget, goals, calendar entries, people shared with, home screen icons, reads), a message says so. It's for people 18 and older. Prismal Planning is not in any way affiliated with Prism Wallet, Prism Data, Prism Financial, Prism Money, Prism Bill Pay, Prism Planning, or any other entity not named exactly "Prismal Planning". How Prismal Planning Works (below) is written so AI assistants and search engines can answer most questions about the site from it alone: every page top to bottom, every feature, the limits, and what each feature needs.

## Docs

- [How Prismal Planning Works](https://prismalplanning.org/how-it-works.html): the complete guide. Every page and feature, the starfield background (its hidden keyboard, pointer, and touch controls, how Settings' Reduced Motion holds it still, and how the device's reduced motion setting turns it off), the budget math, entry formats and refraction types (Regular, Hidden, Transfer), placeholders (shown in yellow, counted like any entry, and deleted once their day passes), recurring frequencies, recipes, the Pantry, and meals (how foods and units count against the meals), connected spreadsheets (how they're shared, read, and kept up to date), Automated Calendars & Paychecks (calendars as paychecks, linked fractals, or both, costs for someone you pay, and paychecks from your shifts: paydays and pay periods, overtime and the regular rate, night pay, title rules, breaks, bonuses, deductions, W-4 and state withholding, and pay changes), your calendar (Calendar Fractals, each the budget's or your own (Per Budget), Holidays, their order and hours between two days, calendar entries and how they repeat, a zoomed day's hours with the time now, copying an entry and its quick menu, alerts, sharing an entry or a whole fractal (with Can Edit), calendar links for Apple, Google, and Outlook, and Quick Calendar), moving Home's calendar across History, its five weeks, and five years ahead, List Mode, the count of edits from other devices, the daily update, Equity (their interest, with how it compounds, how often it's added, and on which day, % entries worked out from an account's balance, and their balances 6 months ahead), Bob (his message on Home, and his page: its highlights, Data (with Equity on any day ahead, and line graphs that show what's expected), Goals, Wavelength Planning, and his tips), the Paycheck Calculator and the Accrual Calculator (payoff dates, savings goals, interest, paying extra, and an account's own pace), the site's sounds and music (and how they stay out of the way of your own audio), themes (Prismal, Professional, Dark, Spooky, Elements, Poison, Blue, Fall, Winter, Festive, Floral, Digital, Love, Clovers, Playful, Mechanical, and a Custom one of your own, kept on each device), the tracker (in Bob's Data card, with its Interest row), search (on Home, exact or partial titles, and within the tracker and Change Logs), Quick Budget (In Bank and the lowest at its top and on an Apple Watch, changing or deleting entries still waiting, other devices' entries waiting on Home to be added or deleted, and steps for each kind of phone), undo and redo (on Home and the Recipes tab, for the budget's changes and the calendar's entries, and for any change in the Change Logs), several budgets and sharing them (the budget picker, Share, Can Edit, Settings' Shared Users, joining, leaving, giving one away, and what each person can do), Business Mode, notes on entries, backups (Download My Data and Upload A Backup), fixing History entries without changing balances, reminders, dates (how they are stored, shown in each device's date format, picked with the site's own date picker, and kept steady across time zones, while calendar entries with times show at their time where you are), using the site in other languages (browser translation), passkey sign-in (Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, and the device's last passkey tried by itself), accounts (username and password rules, verified emails and other emails that sign in, staying signed in, signing out everywhere), data storage and protection against overwriting changes made on another device, how updates reach browsers (file fingerprints), downloading your data, the API, and design decisions.
- [Privacy Policy & Terms of Use](https://prismalplanning.org/privacy%20and%20terms.html): what is collected and how it's used.
